=== B1 (BLOCKING). THE AUTO-QUEUE'S READINESS TEST IS UNSATISFIABLE. 0 OF 5 MERGED PRs WOULD HAVE PASSED IT. ===
scripts/lwb_auto_queue.py::review_records tests a review record's freshness against the RAW pull request head:

    if not head.startswith(reviewed):
        problems.append(f"reviews/{pr}/{name}: reviewed_commit {reviewed[:12]} is not this head")

`head` there is data["head"]["sha"] from the pulls API -- the raw head. But a review record is committed, and that commit advances the raw head past the sha the record names. scripts/lwb_lanes.py states exactly this in resolve_reviewable_head's own docstring -- "committing a review record itself advances the head past the sha that record names, so no committed record could ever match the raw head" -- and solves it by skipping commits that touch only reviews/ and proof/. lwb_auto_queue.py reimplements the comparison WITHOUT that fix, so it can never count a legitimately filed record.

MEASURED against this repository's real history, not argued:
  PR #27 head 19e42b2f7c25 vs reviews/27/cloud-reviewer.json reviewed_commit d85cc34f500e -> no match
  PR #26 head ac89756c9c7c vs reviews/26/independent-verifier.json 967b652          -> no match
  PR #25 head 282b176dc8d9 vs reviews/25/independent-verifier.json 7402b4d          -> no match
  PR #23 head b3cc3583f19f vs reviews/23/independent-verifier.json 4eac900          -> no match
  PR #21 head ad522e7cb930 vs reviews/21/independent-verifier.json 25f7113d721d     -> no match
Five of five PRs that this repository's own merge gate passed and actually merged would have been reported NOT READY by this script, on the reason "reviewed_commit ... is not this head". The same applies to the three open PRs today. When armed, this thing would never enqueue anything.

WHY THE TEST SUITE DOES NOT CATCH IT: tests/test_lwb_auto_queue.py::test_a_fully_satisfied_pr_is_ready uses FakeRepo, whose fixture sets reviewed == HEAD. That state cannot exist in git once the record is committed. The one passing case is built from an input the real system cannot produce, so the suite's green does not bear on whether the script can ever say READY.

THE FIX IS SMALL: resolve the reviewable head the way lwb_lanes does (walk back over commits touching only reviews/ and proof/), or import lwb_lanes.resolve_reviewable_head's rule rather than restating it. Note the script already duplicates REQUIRED_INDEPENDENT_REVIEWS from lwb_lanes deliberately, with a test (test_required_review_count_matches_the_lane_gate) pinning the two together. The head rule is the SECOND thing it duplicates from that module and it has no such test -- and it is the one that was copied wrong.

=== B2 (BLOCKING). A TEST FAILS ON THIS BRANCH, AND lwb-env-leak WOULD GO RED WITH IT. ===
    $ python -m pytest tests/ -q
    FAILED tests/test_lwb_check_env_leak.py::test_success_path_prints_no_needle_count
    1 failed, 514 passed
    $ LWB_PRIVATE_NEEDLES=zzsynth-nothing python scripts/lwb_check_env_leak.py ; echo $?
    FAIL: reviews/29/cloud-reviewer.json:10: absolute path to a python interpreter
    1
The flagged text is not a path. It is the prose "the nine contexts the ruleset requires -- `test` on six os/python pairs", inside reviewer A's own review record on this branch. scripts/lwb_check_env_leak.py:78 is

    r"(?:[A-Za-z]:\\|/)(?:[\w.\-]+[\\/])*python3?(?:\.exe)?(?=[\s\"'`]|$)"

whose leading alternative is a bare "/" and whose path-segment group may match ZERO times, so any "<word>/python" in ordinary English matches. That regex is pre-existing on main and is NOT this PR's defect; the RED TEST IS ON THIS BRANCH and blocks it either way. Two honest repairs: fix the regex to require at least one path segment (main's job, a separate PR), or reword the record's prose to "six os/interpreter pairs" (this branch's job, and it is reviewer A's record, so it is A's to amend -- I will not edit another reviewer's attested record).

=== B3 (BLOCKING). THIS PR HAS NO CI AT ALL, BECAUSE IT CONFLICTS WITH main. ===
    gh api .../pulls/29 -> "mergeable": false, "mergeable_state": "dirty"
    gh api .../commits/24333c2/check-runs -> ONE check run: "decide" (success)
The nine contexts the ruleset requires -- `test` on six os/python legs and `lwb-portable` on three -- have never reported on this head, and cannot: a conflicted PR has no refs/pull/29/merge for a pull_request-triggered workflow to run on. So the only green signal on this PR is the one the PR itself installed, and the required ones are absent rather than red -- exactly the "absent is not passing" distinction the PR's own test_an_absent_required_check_is_not_a_passing_one exists to make.

=== B4 (BLOCKING, AND NOT THE AUTHOR'S DOING). THE HEAD COMMIT PERMANENTLY FAILS lwb-commit-identity. ===
    $ git log -1 --format='%an <%ae>' 24333c2
    LEAPWare-HQ <manny.ramos@followoz.com>
    $ python scripts/lwb_check_commit_identity.py --base <live main> --head HEAD ; echo $?
    FAIL: commit author not LEAPWare or an allow-listed bot: LEAPWare-HQ <manny.ramos@followoz.com>
    1
ALLOWED_HUMAN is exactly ("LEAPWare", "leapware@outlook.com"). 24333c2 is reviewer A's own record commit. Force-push is denied in this repository, so it cannot be corrected in place: as it stands #29 needs a re-cut, the same repair #35 was cut for and #31 before it. I hit the identical defect on #35 (861ee7d) and #32 (4305428) in this same run -- three open PRs, all three poisoned by the same routine's commits in the same hour.
THE STRUCTURAL CAUSE, which is worth more than the three repairs: lwb_lanes.resolve_reviewable_head EXCLUDES record-only commits, deliberately, so a record cannot invalidate itself -- but lwb_check_commit_identity._authors INCLUDES every commit in the range with no exemption at all. The two gates disagree about whether a reviewer's own commit counts, and the routine that exists to unblock a PR can therefore permanently red it. I am charging this as blocking on the PR because the PR cannot merge with it, not as a fault in the PR's content.

=== NON-BLOCKING NB1. THE TEST THAT PROVES THE WORKFLOW GUARD IS NOT VACUOUS DOES NOT TEST THE GUARD. ===
I nearly filed this as blocking and the probe stopped me, so I am recording both halves.
41c1690 fixed a genuinely vacuous guard (its predecessor asked whether "default_branch" appeared anywhere in the workflow text, and the string appeared in the comment warning about that very hazard). THE REPLACEMENT GUARD IS GENUINELY NOT VACUOUS -- I introduced the real hazard into the real workflow file (added a `pull_request:` trigger beside the existing push trigger) and test_the_workflow_never_checks_out_pull_request_code_under_a_write_token FAILED, as it should. Credit where it is due; my expectation was wrong.
What it does not do is protect itself. test_that_guard_actually_fails_when_the_hazard_is_introduced RE-IMPLEMENTS the predicate inline over a hand-built dict instead of calling the guard. Probe, two stages, both with the hazard present in the real workflow file:
    (A) guard intact  -> test_the_workflow_never_checks_out... FAILED, test_that_guard_actually_fails... passed
    (B) guard gutted (pr_driven = set()) -> BOTH PASSED
So a future weakening of the guard is invisible to the test whose stated purpose is "proves the guard above is not vacuous, which is the whole point". Have it call the guard function, or parametrise one predicate that both tests use. Working tree restored from copies and `git status --porcelain` verified empty afterwards.

=== NON-BLOCKING NB2. "I COULD NOT CHECK" AND "I CHECKED AND FOUND NOTHING" SHARE A REPRESENTATION, IN THE FILE THAT PROMISES THEY DO NOT. ===
The module docstring says: "Exits 0 when it reached a decision (ready or not ready) and 1 only when it could NOT decide -- an unreachable API, an unreadable record. 'I could not check' never shares an exit code with 'I checked and found nothing'." Both _list_dir and _contents_json call _gh with allow_fail=True, which swallows EVERY non-zero gh exit -- 403, 404, 500, a proxy refusal, a timed-out token -- and returns "".
    (stubbed subprocess.run -> returncode 22, stderr "gh: HTTP 403: Resource not accessible")
    _list_dir("reviews/29", ref)      -> []
    _contents_json("proof/29.json", ref) -> None
    review_records(29, head)          -> (0, ['no review records under reviews/29/ at aaaaaaaaaaaa'])
A total API blackout is reported as the affirmative fact that the PR has no review records and no proof record, at EXIT_DECIDED. The direction of harm is safe (it refuses to enqueue, never wrongly enqueues) and that is why this is not blocking -- but the docstring's claim is false as written, and the repo's named defect pattern is present in the layer that advertises immunity to it. test_an_unreadable_record_raises_rather_than_reading_as_absent covers only unparseable JSON CONTENT, not an unreachable API. Fix: distinguish 404 from every other failure in _gh (gh exits 1 with "Not Found" for a 404; anything else should raise CouldNotCheck).

=== NON-BLOCKING NB3. reviews/29/ CARRIES TWO RECORDS THAT NAME RECORD-ONLY COMMITS. ===
cloud-reviewer.json names 25b0801 and cloud-reviewer-3.json names 8a83970; both are reviews/-only commits, so neither can ever equal the reviewable head ae29b1a and both are STALE by reviews/README.md's own rule. Only cloud-reviewer-2.json (ae29b1a) is bound to a reviewable head. All three are DISAGREE, so nothing turns on it today, but a record must name the REVIEWABLE head, not the raw one. Worth stating because independent_reviews appends an error for EVERY invalid record in the directory: one malformed record fails the job even when a valid one sits beside it, so a second reviewer's record can only ever hurt.
